OpenAI 新模型撞名「Sol、Terra、Luna」，Solana 官方爆笑神評：Sam Altcoinman
AI 巨頭 OpenAI 剛發布最新 GPT-5.6 系列模型，沒想到卻意外在加密貨幣社群引發一場迷因狂歡！由於新模型命名為「Sol、Terra、Luna」，不僅直接撞名公鏈 Solana，更喚起了幣圈人對 2022 年 LUNA 崩盤的恐懼。Solana 官方帳號火速在貼文下神回覆一句「Sam Altcoinman」，幽默嘲諷執行長 Sam Altman 宛如在發山寨幣，瞬間引爆社群朝聖。
OpenAI 正式發表 GPT-5.6 家族！一文拆解 Sol、Terra 與 Luna 三款模型與定價
紐約時報：OpenAI 傾向推遲 IPO 至 2027 年，Sam Altman 要求估值須達一兆美元
工智慧與加密貨幣的跨界碰撞，有時候只需要一個巧妙的命名巧合。2026 年 6 月 26 日，OpenAI 盛大宣布推出下一代前沿模型 GPT-5.6 系列，並將旗下的三款模型分別命名為
Sol（旗艦）、Terra（平衡）與 Luna（親民）
這份看似充滿「日月星辰」宇宙浪漫色彩的命名，在加密貨幣投資人的眼裡，卻完全是另一幅光景。
在幣圈的語境中，「Sol」是當紅高效能公鏈 Solana 的代幣代稱；而「Terra」與「Luna」這兩個名字湊在一起，則是所有加密投資人心中永遠的痛 —— 2022 年引發數百億美元蒸發、震驚全球的 Terra/LUNA 死亡螺旋崩盤事件。
OpenAI 這波無心插柳的命名，立刻讓敏銳的 Crypto 社群嗅到了絕佳的迷因（Meme）素材，而第一個開槍的，正是 Solana 官方。
Solana 官方神吐槽：Sam Altcoinman
面對 OpenAI 的官方公告，Solana 官方 X 帳號（@solana）毫不遲疑地留下了一句極度簡短、卻殺傷力十足的回覆：
這個精妙的諧音梗將 OpenAI 執行長 Sam Altman 的姓氏，巧妙改編成了「Altcoinman（山寨幣/迷因幣男人）」。Solana 官方用最簡潔的方式，幽默調侃了 OpenAI 這次的模型發布簡直就像是一個「發幣專案（Crypto Project）」，而 Altman 本人就是這個專案的發幣大佬。
勾起 LUNA 崩盤 PTSD，社群迷因大爆發
這則精準抓緊時事的社群回覆，發布後迅速累積超過 9 萬次觀看與兩千多個讚，並在留言區引發了一場迷因接力賽。許多網友笑著表示：「Sol 奇點要來了（The solgularity is coming）」，將 AI 的奇點理論與 Solana 結合在一起。
不過，更多網友則是對「Terra」和「Luna」這兩個名字感到崩潰與恐懼。有網友開玩笑地留言：「看到 Terra 和 Luna 放在一起，我的加密貨幣 PTSD（創傷後壓力症候群）直接發作」、「這三款模型的意思是：Sol 會暴漲，而 Terra 和 Luna 會歸零嗎？」
這場由命名巧合引發的社群狂歡，不僅展現了加密貨幣社群極強的造梗能力與自嘲精神，也意外為 OpenAI 的新模型發布，在科技圈之外帶來了龐大的免費社群流量。

Anthropic 解禁最強模型 Mythos 5 但「僅供美國政府使用」！網怒轟雙標，Fable 5 慘遭持續封殺
AI 巨頭 Anthropic 於今（27）日發布最新公告，宣布在與美國政府斡旋半個月後，其最強大的網路安全模型「Claude Mythos 5」已獲准重新上線，但存取權「僅限」提供給負責維護美國關鍵基礎設施的特定組織，大眾版 Fable 5 則仍在爭取解禁中。這份公告隨即引爆社群公關災難，逾百萬名網友痛批 Anthropic 自導自演 AI 恐懼，最終淪為政府壟斷前沿技術的特權打手。
以「安全」為名狂攬權力？解密 Anthropic 矛盾心理：只有我們稱霸，世界才安全
Anthropic 指控阿里發動「史上最大克隆攻擊」，狂刷 Claude 2,880 萬次
譽為「網路核武」的最強人工智慧模型，終究還是落入了少數機構的手中。在經歷了 6 月 12 日突遭美國政府限制存取的風波後，AI 新創巨頭 Anthropic 於今（27）日首度公開了旗下前沿模型 Claude Mythos 5 與 Fable 5 的最新解禁進度，然而結果卻讓廣大開發者社群大失所望。
Since June 12, we’ve been working closely with the US government to restore access to Claude Mythos 5 and Fable 5. Today, the government notified us that Mythos 5, our strongest cybersecurity model, can be redeployed to a set of US organizations that operate and defend critical…
— Anthropic (@AnthropicAI)
Mythos 5 有條件回歸，Fable 5 仍遭封殺
根據 Anthropic 官方在 X 平台（原推特）發布的聲明，公司自 6 月 12 日以來，一直積極與美國政府密切合作以尋求解套。官方表示：「今天，政府通知我們，我們最強大的網路安全模型
，可以重新部署給一批負責營運和防護關鍵基礎設施的美國組織。」
Anthropic 強調，團隊正以最快速度為這些「特定組織」恢復存取權。至於原先面向大眾的 Fable 5 模型，官方坦言目前仍無法提供服務，僅表示將「繼續與政府合作擴大 Mythos 5 的存取範圍，並努力讓 Fable 5 再次開放給一般使用。」
社群炸鍋：炒作 AI 恐懼只為建立「技術特權」
這篇原意為更新進度的公告，卻在發布後引發了史詩級的公關災難。截至目前，該貼文已突破 130 萬次觀看，但留言區幾乎一面倒地充滿了憤怒與抨擊。加密貨幣與開源社群對這種「規則只適用於平民（Rules for thee but not for me）」的雙重標準感到極度不滿。
許多強烈批評指出，Anthropic 長期以來不斷在市場上散播「AI 毀滅論」與過度強調安全風險的敘事，成功引起了華盛頓當局的恐慌與監管介入。然而，最終的結果並非讓技術變得更安全，而是名正言順地將最先進的 AI 算力與技術壟斷在美國軍政機構與少數特權階級手中，一般企業與平民卻被以「安全」為由剝奪了使用權。
這起事件再次凸顯了當前 AI 產業的核心矛盾：當科技巨頭高舉「造福全人類」的大旗時，他們實質上可能正在協助國家機器打造一道難以跨越的技術高牆。
Anthropic 前研究員創辦 Mirendil 募得 2 億鎂，號稱「能自我升級的AI」
Anthropic 控阿里巴巴「非法竊取」Claude：2880 萬次對話、近 2.5 萬假帳號，蒸餾戰火燒進美國議院

OpenAI 正式發表 GPT-5.6 家族！一文拆解 Sol、Terra 與 Luna 三款模型與定價
OpenAI 今（26）日正式公開其下一代前沿大模型「GPT-5.6 系列」，並破天荒採取「三位一體」的多模型家族策略，推出旗艦 Sol、平價 Terra 以及高速 Luna 三款模型。其中，Sol 具備極強的長時程網路安全漏洞研究與「超強代理（Ultra Mode）」能力，在多項基準測試中將對手 Anthropic 的 Claude Mythos 遠遠甩在後頭。
OpenAI 新模型 GPT-5.6 不給上：川普政府要求分階段發布
紐約時報：OpenAI 傾向推遲 IPO 至 2027 年，Sam Altman 要求估值須達一兆美元
全球開發者與企業熱烈期盼下，AI 領頭羊 OpenAI 於今日（26 日）拋出了投向市場的重磅炸彈，正式發表其下一代前沿模型系列「GPT-5.6 家族」。本次 OpenAI 改變了過往單一模型的升級路徑，改採全新命名系統，一次性推出「日月星辰」三款鎖定不同場景的能力階層模型。
Introducing a limited preview of GPT-5.6 Sol, our next generation frontier model, as well as GPT-5.6 Terra, a balanced model for efficient, everyday work, and GPT-5.6 Luna, a fast and affordable model for high-volume work.
https://t.co/OoM83SyISN
日月地「三模型家族」降臨，Sol Ultra 創下 SOTA 新紀錄
，新命名系統中，數字 5.6 代表世代，而 Sol、Terra、Luna 則代表不同的能力階層，未來將各自獨立推進，讓用戶能在智能、速度與成本之間做出最完美的權衡：
：家族中的終極旗艦模型。相比 GPT-5.5 有著跨越式的性能突破，專門為極其複雜的「自主代理工作（Agentic work）」而生。
：日常工作平衡型模型。其性能與前代 GPT-5.5 相當，但運行成本直接暴降 2 倍，是企業高效日常應用的首選。
：高產量、極速且最親民的模型。在提供強大基礎能力的同時，將成本壓到最低，適合大規模重複性的高容量工作。
在功能層面，旗艦級的 Sol 引入了全新的
`max` reasoning effort
功能，賦予模型進行深度、長時間推理的餘裕；此外，全新的
則允許 Sol 呼叫多個「子代理（Subagents）」協同作戰。在命令列工作流基準測試
的全新世界紀錄（SOTA），大幅領先競爭對手 Anthropic 的 Claude Mythos 5。
史上最強網路安全模型，70 萬小時自動化紅隊壓測
除了程式碼與基因組定量分析外，GPT-5.6 Sol 最令人矚目的突破在於其驚人的「網路安全（Cybersecurity）」能力。Sol 是目前 OpenAI 在安全領域最強的模型，能處理長視野的漏洞研究與利用任務。在 ExploitBench 基準測試中，Sol 僅需耗費對手 Mythos Preview 約 1/3 的輸出 tokens，就能達到同等甚至更優異的漏洞挖掘成果。
為了防堵高風險的網路犯罪濫用，OpenAI 推出了至今最強的分層安全防護堆疊。該模型經歷了數週的人類紅隊測試，並通過了高達
70 萬 A100 等效 GPU 小時的自動化紅隊壓測
，內建即時分類器、帳戶級審查與主動防護暗門。雖然 Sol 能在 Chromium 和 Firefox 中精準找出未知漏洞，但報告顯示它尚不具備自主產生端到端完整攻擊鏈的能力，因此未越過「關鍵網路威脅」的紅線。
前沿旗艦、極致智能、超強代理（Ultra Mode）與網絡核防禦
高CP值中階、等同 GPT-5.5 性能但成本直接降低 2 倍
親民極速、適合海量吞吐與日常自動化工作流程
（備註：Sol 最低快取定價為每百萬 Tokens $0.50，全系列支援最少 30 分鐘生命週期的明確快取斷點。）
雖然性能令人驚艷，但許多急著體驗的開發者可能要再等一等。OpenAI 透露，目前該系列模型正處於
「有限預覽（Limited Preview）」
階段，僅透過 API 和 Codex 開放給少數受信任的合作夥伴。這背後的原因相當具有政治意味 —— 由於其強大的網路安全敏感度，OpenAI 目前正接受美國政府因應網路安全行政命令框架的合規審查，參與預覽的名單也已同步分享給官方。
儘管面臨監管阻力，OpenAI 重申反對將政府的長期審查程序「常態化」，認為這會阻礙企業和網路防禦者取得最佳工具。公司計畫在未來幾週內，將 GPT-5.6 家族全面普及至所有 ChatGPT 與 API 用戶。此外，自 7 月起，GPT-5.6 Sol 將與 Cerebras 晶片強強聯手，為指定客戶提供高達每秒 750 tokens 的史詩級推理超高速，再度宣示其無法動搖的 AI 霸權。

Collector Crypt 晉升鏈上「印鈔機」：活躍用戶不足千人，巨鯨撐起 97% 收入
Collector Crypt 強勢躋身 Solana 收入前段班，更一度衝上全網協議收入 Top 10。本文解析鏈上 TCG（集換式卡牌遊戲）因何逆勢崛起、Solana 憑什麼吃下逾 8 成市場，以及 CARDS 代幣、巨鯨資金與扭蛋機制如何推動這波熱潮爆發。
近期，集換式卡牌遊戲（TCG）項目 Collector Crypt 強勢闖入全網收入榜 Top10，並一度登頂 Solana 收入最高協議，引發社群熱議。
當大多數加密項目仍在熊市中艱難求生時，Collector Crypt 卻憑藉著強勁的獲利能力，成為市場中少數的印鈔機。以 Collector Crypt 為代表的代幣化 TCG 賽道，正將收藏和抽卡的樂趣搬到鏈上，快速搶佔加密市場的注意力。
鏈上 TCG 正在「跑贏」NFT？ Solana 吃下八成市場
自去年以來，融合 IP 、收藏、社交與遊戲屬性的 TCG 正進入新一輪成長週期，市場熱度持續攀升。
這股 TCG 熱潮也開始往鏈上遷移。自 2025 年以來，加密市場陸續湧現出一批代幣化 TCG 玩家，包括 Collector Crypt 、 Phygitals 、 Courtyard 、 Ready Cards 、 Beezie 等。
相較於傳統實體卡牌，代幣化 TCG 在流動性與交易效率上顯著提升，同時降低了假卡與盜竊等風險，尤其在高價值卡牌優勢更為明顯，但由於高度依賴中心化金庫和託管體系，也引發市場擔憂，若平台倒閉或金庫出問題可能造成資產損失。
為解決上述問題，部分鏈上平台開始引進更完善的實體錨定與風控機制。例如，Collector Crypt 在美國蒙大拿州設有約 2.8 萬平方英尺的實體倉儲保險庫，用於存放真實卡牌資產，並透過 PSA 等評級體系進行認證與背書，以增強資產透明度與用戶信任。
受益於實體收藏市場的持續繁榮以及資產代幣化需求成長，鏈上 TCG 市場近幾個月進入快速成長階段，成為當前加密熊市中成長較為明顯的細分賽道之一。
Artemis 數據顯示，2026 年 6 月，鏈上 TCG 市場交易額突破 4.9 億美元，較去年同期翻了 7.6 倍；每月活躍用戶約 5300 人，較去年增長約 253.3%；各協議月度累計收入約 1180 萬美元，較去年同期翻了 1.8 倍以上。
反觀 NFT 賽道，CryptoSlam 數據顯示，同期 NFT 市場的交易額約 1.5 億美元。儘管兩者均屬於鏈上數位收藏資產，但 TCG 展現出更高的用戶參與意願與交易活躍度，主要原因在於其兼具實體卡牌的真實價值支撐、競技與遊戲屬性帶來的持續使用場景，以及鏈上交易賦予的高流動性、資產可組合性和全球化流通能力。
從公鏈生態來看，目前代幣化 TCG 專案主要部署於 Solana 、 BNB Chain 、 Polygon 、 Base 等主流公鏈，其中 Solana 憑藉著技術優勢、先發效應以及爆款應用 Collector Crypt，已成為代幣化 TCG 的核心戰場。根據 Artemis 數據顯示，Solana 已佔據鏈上 TCG 市場 80.8% 的份額，遠超其他公鏈，成為當前代幣化 TCG 最活躍、最具流動性的生態。
不過，從整體市場來看，鏈上 TCG 仍處於發展早期。根據 Global Market Insights 報告預計，全球 TCG 市場規模在 2026 年預計達到或已跨越約 92 億美元，預計到 2035 年市值將達 169 億美元。
相較於龐大的實體市場，目前鏈上 TCG 的滲透率仍然有限，也意味著在資產上鍊、交易基礎設施及全球流動性方面仍具備較大的成長空間。
Collector Crypt 一家獨大，97% 的收入卻靠巨鯨撐起
本輪鏈上 TCG 賽道的爆發式成長，離不開 Collector Crypt 的推動。作為當前賽道最具統治力的項目，其在交易規模、收入能力以及市場份額上，已與其他平台拉開明顯差距。
Artemis 數據顯示，自上線以來，Collector Crypt 累計交易額已突破 14 億美元，累計協議收入達 6,800 萬美元，遠超其他鏈上 TCG 平台。
從近一週的市場表現來看，Collector Crypt 交易金額約為 1.27 億美元，佔整個鏈上 TCG 市場的 74.3%；同期，其他平台的交易金額大多僅為數百萬美元甚至更低。收入方面，Collector Crypt 單週協議收入約 520 萬美元，而其他平台普遍僅有數萬美元，部分甚至處於虧損狀態。
除了持續擴大在鏈上 TCG 賽道的領先優勢，Collector Crypt 的獲利能力也開始躋身整個加密產業第一梯隊。
近期，Collector Crypt 與 Tether 、 Circle 、 Hyperliquid 等協議一同進入全網協議收入排行榜前十，已經具備與 DeFi 、穩定幣等成熟賽道頭部項目競爭的商業化能力。同時，根據 DeFiLlama 數據，截至 6 月 26 日，Collector Crypt 已成為 Solana 收入排名第二的協議，僅次於 Meme 印鈔機 Pump.fun 。
事實上，今年以來，Collector Crypt 幾乎所有核心​​經營指標都進入快速成長階段。
Artemis 數據顯示，今年 6 月，平台的月交易額突破 3.3 億美元，相較於 1 月的 9,750 萬美元成長約 3.4 倍；同期月活躍用戶由 276 人成長至 735 人，成長約 2.6 倍；協議營收則由 440 萬美元成長至 1,340 萬美元，成長超過 3 倍。
不過，Collector Crypt 快速成長的同時，也面臨獲利能力承壓的問題。 Blockworks 數據顯示，截至 6 月 26 日，平台累計實現總收入 7.07 億美元，但淨收入僅 4,633 萬美元，營收留存率約 6.5% 。同時，受高價低毛利卡包佔比上升以及極高即時回購率等因素影響，Collector Crypt 平台毛利率持續走低，截至 6 月 24 日已降至 2.74%，較年初的 6.03% 明顯下滑。
不僅如此，從使用者架構來看，Collector Crypt 的收入仍高度依賴少數高淨值玩家，堪稱鏈上 TCG 的「巨鯨樂園」。
Dune 數據顯示，過去六個月，平台約有 14,594 名鏈上付費用戶，共貢獻近 5 億美元交易額。其中，消費超過 100 萬美元的玩家僅 80 名（佔總用戶 0.6%），貢獻了 51.8% 的收入；消費 10 萬至 100 萬美元的用戶有 522 名（佔 3.6%），貢獻了收入的 35.6%；消費 1 萬至 10 萬美元的用戶（佔 10.4%）則佔了 9.7% 的收入。相較之下，佔用戶總數超 42.1% 、消費低於 250 美元的用戶，僅貢獻約 0.1% 的收入。也就是說，目前 Collector Crypt 有約 14.6% 的用戶，貢獻了平台約 97.1% 的營收。
這種高度集中的收入結構，一方面反映出 Collector Crypt 高淨值用戶具備較強的支付能力和消費粘性，為平台帶來了可觀的盈利能力，但也難以完全排除刷量行為；另一方面，這也意味著平台若要實現可持續的規模化增長，仍需拓展用戶群交易，降低對少數巨鯨群體的依賴度。
日活不足千人，Collector Crypt 憑何躋身收入前十名？
推動 Collector Crypt 交易爆發的重要原因之一，就是平台推出的鏈上扭蛋機制（Gacha）。此模式借鑒了傳統 TCG 的拆卡玩法，透過隨機獎勵、稀缺卡牌和即時回饋，不斷放大玩家的期待感與重複消費意願，成為平台交易成長的核心引擎。
目前，Collector Crypt 已成為 Solana 最大的鏈上扭蛋市場，佔據約 87.4% 的市場。
Blockworks 和 Artemis 數據分別顯示，僅 6 月份，平台扭蛋交易額便達到 1.27 億美元，幾乎貢獻了平台全部交易額；同期累計開包價值突破 1 億美元，較年初接近翻倍。同時，參與人數也持續增加。截至 6 月 23 日，平台日活躍扭蛋用戶已達 811 人，而此前數月通常不足 300 人。
值得注意的是，Collector Crypt 的高交易額不僅源自於活躍度提升，更得益於前文提到的巨鯨用戶持續貢獻的大額消費。 Blockworks 數據顯示，每位用戶平均扭蛋消費金額高達 7,829 美元，近兩個月一度升至 9,858 美元。
除了扭蛋機制，寶可夢 IP 與代幣經濟模型也成為 Collector Crypt 持續成長的重要推手。
其中，寶可夢 IP 是平台最核心的流量來源。 Blockworks 數據顯示，今年 6 月，Collector Crypt 平台代幣化收藏品價值（TCV）達 2,610 萬美元，其中約 73.8% 來自寶可夢卡牌。在熱門開包產品中，約 76% 的卡包均為寶可夢系列，其中售價 1,000 美元的寶可夢禮包佔全部開包量近一半。換言之，優質 IP 仍是驅動用戶消費與交易的重要基礎。
另一方面，CARDS 代幣建構起平台成長飛輪。自上線以來，Collector Crypt 累計向社群釋放 4.75% 的 CARDS 供應量，其中包括 TGE 階段 2.5% 的初始空投，以及三輪季度空投，每輪釋放 0.75%，最近一次季度空投價值約 400 萬美元。
相較於單純的空投激勵，Collector Crypt 也建立了雙重回購機制：一方面，對卡牌資產進行即時回購，為交易提供持續流動性；另一方面，則利用協議收入持續回購 CARDS 代幣，以增強代幣價值支撐。
隨著平台交易持續成長，協議收入同步增加，CARDS 回購規模也隨之擴大；而代幣價格上漲進一步刺激用戶參與交易、開包和持有意願，進而形成飛輪效應。
受此影響，CoinGecko 數據顯示，今年以來 CARDS 累計漲幅已超過 412%，目前 FDV 已達 5.1 億美元。近期，Arthur Hayes 旗下家族辦公室 Maelstrom 更在研究報告中更是給予 CARDS 夏季末期 4 美元的目標價，進一步提升了市場關注度。
值得一提的是，根據 Maelstrom Fund 分析師 Lukas Ruppert 報告披露，Collector Crypt 營運中心相關錢包已累計變現 4,570 萬美元 USDC 。
需要注意的是，代幣 CARDS 將迎來持續解鎖。目前，Collector Crypt 已完成約 23.6% 的代幣解鎖，剩餘代幣將持續鎖定至 2027 年 11 月。其中，下一次解鎖將於 6 月 29 日進行，預計釋放約 2,884 萬枚 CARDS，價值約 746 萬美元；此外，官方近期披露，一家 Pre-Seed 輪早期投資者已透過場外交易向某流動性基金出售約 150 萬美元 CARDS 代幣。
隨著營運資金流出、代幣持續解鎖以及早期籌碼開始兌現收益，市場流通籌碼將逐步增加，投資者需持續關注短期潛在的市場拋壓。
整體來看，Collector Crypt 的崛起驗證了鏈上 TCG 商業模式的可行性，也推動這條賽道進入快速發展階段。不過，鏈上 TCG 仍處於早期發展階段，無論是用戶拓展、資產供給，或是基礎設施等方面仍有較大的成長空間。

《CLARITY 法案》7 月表決倒數！4 大未解問題卡關，過關機率跌破 5 成
美國國會計劃於 7 月加速推進《數位資產市場清晰法案（Clarity Act）》，但因會期僅剩 4 週，且面臨高官道德、DeFi 豁免等 4 大核心爭議未解，今年通過率已降至 48%。
關注美國加密監管的獨立記者 Eleanor Terrett 在 6 月 26 日
《數位資產市場清晰法案》（Clarity Act）
這股急迫感主要受到美國住房法案爭議帶來的政治壓力，以及國會剩餘時間無多的現實所推動。 Terrett 指出，參議員在 7 月 13 日結束休會返回華盛頓後，在 8 月夏季休會前將僅剩 20 個工作天，只剩大約 4 週的時間能將該法案送交參議院表決，並返回眾議院。
與此同時，美國眾議院金融服務委員會先前已宣布，數位資產、金融科技和 AI 小組委員會預計於 7 月 17 日在紐約舉辦一場名為
「構建金融未來：《清晰法案》如何釋放創新」
🚨NEW: There is a renewed sense of urgency among GOP lawmakers to get the Clarity Act passed, I’m told.
It’s being driven by heightened political pressure following the fallout from the Housing bill, as well as the realization that time is running short.
When senators return…

— Eleanor Terrett (@EleanorTerrett)
雖然議員們在 6 月底離開華盛頓前，仍有包含道德條款在內的關鍵議題未達成共識，
但《The Block》報導指出，參議院助理透露，《清晰法案》在 7 月將成為民主黨與共和黨共同的優先事項。
參議員盧米斯（Cynthia Lummis）接受福斯商業頻道採訪時預估，
談判代表將在 7 月 4 日左右公布最終的折衷文本，並在 7 月中正式推動法案表決。
然而，美國國會議程正面臨其他重大法案的強烈擠壓。
據《CoinDesk》報導，美國總統川普突然拒簽獲得跨黨派支持的住房法案。該法案原本包含一項至 2030 年底前、為期 4 年的央行數位貨幣（CBDC）禁止條款，深受加密貨幣產業支持。
川普的主張是，在國會通過要求選民投票時出示公民身分證明的《拯救美國法案》（SAVE America Act）之前，他將擱置其他立法。眾議院議長 Mike Johnson 隨後表示，將嘗試把該項選民身分法案納入其他預算案中。
川普的這項舉動引發連鎖反應，打亂了國會的既定節奏。 TD Cowen 政策分析師 Jaret Seiberg 分析，由於參議院共和黨人不太可能取消阻礙議事表決的機制，該選民身分法案在參議院過關的機率極低。
加密產業消息人士透露，川普的拒絕簽署為國會增添了更多不確定性，民主黨人因而產生信任危機，認為不論達成何種協議都有可能隨時被推翻，且國會內部已出現立法疲勞。
另外，參議院在 7 月還必須處理國防授權法案、每 5 年更新一次且影響廣泛的農業法案，以及川普政府對聯邦住房金融局局長 Bill Pulte 兼任國家情報總監等爭議性人事任命案，這就讓《清晰法案》在有限的院會時間中，面臨激烈的排程競爭。
《CoinDesk》分析指出，即便立法進程受到威脅，但《清晰法案》目前仍有 4 個核心面向的談判尚未完成：
民主黨參議員 Ruben Gallego 與 Kirsten Gillibrand 等人，正與共和黨及白宮進行三方會談。
民主黨人強烈批評川普家族涉入加密貨幣業務 WLF ，並從中獲利超過 10 億美元的行為。
對此，白宮顧問 Patrick Witt 曾提議擴大限制官員範圍，避免直接針對總統個人。
路透揭露伊朗交易所與川普 WLF「間接關係」：靠 BNB 、波場鏈處理 23 億鎂
然而，由於共和黨與白宮隨後撤回一項授權州檢察總長在司法部未能執行道德規則時提起訴訟的條款，導致 6 月 9 日的跨黨派道德談判陷入僵局，至今仍未達成共識。
法案中的《區塊鏈監管確定性法案》條款旨在澄清非託管開發者不屬於貨幣傳輸者，雖然受到產業支持，但民主黨參議員 Catherine Cortez Masto 對此持續表達反對，並要求修改。
執法部門與天主教會領袖也擔憂，這會削弱打擊人口販運等犯罪的工具。參議員盧米斯對此回應，法案已包含 1 億 5,000 萬美元的專款用於打擊非法加密活動。
DeFi 開發者曙光？美國 SEC：特定加密交易介面，可豁免註冊經紀商
參議院農業委員會的民主黨人，正要求確保補齊商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）的兩個民主黨委員空缺。
銀行業與加密產業在穩定幣回饋收益上的爭執仍在持續。雖然參議員 Angela Alsobrooks 和 Thom Tillis 在上個月已達成折衷版本，限制回饋與帳戶餘額直接掛鉤，
但美國銀行家協會與摩根大通執行長 Jamie Dimon 依然公開表達強烈反對，並計劃杯葛法案。
加密法案僵持中！摩根大通反對穩定幣利息，美議員：再不過就輸給中國
若錯失 8 月休會前空窗期，恐延宕至 2030 年
面對緊迫的日程，加密貨幣產業正面全力衝刺。數位商會執行長 Cody Carbone 表示， Hyperliquid 、 Elliptic 和 Anchorage Digital 等加密企業成員已組成 50 人的代表團，前往國會山莊拜會約 30 名尚未表態的議員辦公室爭取支持。
另外，區塊鏈協會也與 160 名美國前國家安全、情報和執法領域的專業人士聯名致信參議院多數黨領袖 John Thune 與民主黨領袖 Chuck Schumer，強調通過法案對國家安全的重要性。
區塊鏈協會執行長、前 CFTC  委員 Summer Mersinger 則抱持樂觀態度，認為目前的各項爭議都是可以解決的，7 月表決依然是可實現的目標。
圖源：financial-planning ｜區塊鏈協會執行長、前 CFTC  委員 Summer Mersinger
預測市場 Polymarket 交易員對於《清晰法案》在 2026 年通過的勝率，已從上個月的 74% 下滑至目前的 48%，Galaxy Research 則評估過關機率約為 50%
盧米斯也警告，若國會錯過 8 月休會前的窗口，隨著 11 月期中選舉臨近，法案將被迫延宕至年底的跛腳鴨會期，甚至可能因國會結構重組，導致被推遲到 2030 年。
金融改革組織「美國人爭取金融改革」（AFR）副主任 Mark Hays 也指出，多數美國人更關心涉及食品與農業援助的農業法案，而非這項由少數富裕利益團體推動的非主流議題。如果法案今年未能通過，明年 1 月將在新一屆國會重新啟動。

比特幣何時見底？分析師看跌至 5.5 萬美元、 ETP 資金流首度轉負
比特幣跌破 6 萬美元，分析指受美元走強與 ETP 資金首度轉負影響，價格恐再下探 5.5 萬美元，市場態度正趨於保守。
10x Research：比特幣仍可能下探 5.5 萬美元
比特幣（$BTC）短暫跌破 6 萬美元後，市場對於何時見底的討論迅速升溫。
10x Research 創辦人 Markus Thielen 認為，比特幣可能尚未完成本輪修正，價格仍有機會下探至 5.5 萬美元附近，之後才有望形成較穩固的底部。
Thielen 指出，目前市場同時面臨美元走強、聯準會政策維持偏鷹、風險資產買盤降溫，以及市場槓桿部位尚未完全出清等壓力。若總體經濟環境持續影響市場流動性，加密貨幣短期內恐怕仍將承受修正壓力。
隨著市場重新評估風險，5.5 萬美元也成為不少交易員關注的下一個重要支撐區間。若價格跌至該位置，將較 6 萬美元再回落約 8％，也可能進一步考驗中長期投資人的持有信心。
資金面也出現新的警訊。 K33 Research 數據顯示，比特幣 ETP 的滾動一年資金流量已轉為負值，這是自 2023 年以來首次出現流出金額超過流入金額的情況。
圖源：K33 Research ｜ 比特幣 ETP 的滾動一年資金流量已轉為負值
過去一年，現貨 ETF 與各類 ETP 一直是推動比特幣上漲的重要資金來源。如今年度資金流由正轉負，顯示機構投資人的配置意願正在降溫，也反映市場對風險資產的態度趨於保守。
K33 Research 研究主管 Vetle Lunde 表示，比特幣 ETP 持倉已較高點減少約 8％，無論從持倉規模或資金流向來看，都顯示市場正進入調整階段。
比特幣持續走弱，也讓市場重新討論過去備受關注的百萬美元價格預測。
Barstool Sports 創辦人 Dave Portnoy 近期
，當比特幣跌破 6 萬美元後，他開始懷疑市場對比特幣最終上看 100 萬美元的預測是否過於樂觀。他認為，短期市場仍存在許多不確定因素，投資人應重新評估目前的風險，而非完全依賴長線價格目標。
people who say it’s going to a million and how it’s the future to tell me why all the people who have always said it’s a scam and going to zero are wrong.   Cause it seems like it’s going to zero
— Dave Portnoy (@stoolpresidente)
Portnoy 的發言反映部分散戶投資人的情緒變化。過去市場熱絡時，百萬美元等長期目標經常成為討論焦點；近期行情持續修正後，市場關注焦點逐漸轉向資金流、流動性與支撐價位，交易策略也變得更加保守。
除了價格走勢之外，市場目前更關注資金是否重新流入。若 ETF 與 ETP 恢復淨流入，美國市場現貨買盤回升，加上槓桿部位完成清理，都有助於市場逐步建立新的支撐。
另一方面，持有大量比特幣的 Strategy 股價近期同步下跌，也反映市場開始重新評估加密資產相關企業的風險。比特幣價格修正已影響 ETF 、 ETP 、挖礦公司及財庫型企業，市場波動也從加密貨幣本身擴散至相關股票。
目前投資人仍持續觀察比特幣能否重新站回 6 萬美元，以及 5.5 萬美元附近是否出現明顯承接買盤。若資金流向改善，市場信心有機會逐步修復；若賣壓持續增加，價格仍可能進一步測試更低支撐區間。

比特幣恐再跌 30%！江卓爾：熊市底部落在 4.2 萬至 4.4 萬美元
比特幣還沒跌完？萊比特礦池（LeBit）創辦人江卓爾近日拋出最新市場預測，認為本輪熊市低點最快將於 2026 年第四季出現，屆時比特幣可能下探 4.2 萬至 4.4 萬美元，較目前幣價約 6 萬美元仍有 30% 的下跌空間。
比特幣還沒跌完？萊比特礦池（LeBit）創辦人江卓爾近日拋出最新
，認為本輪熊市低點最快將於 2026 年第四季出現，屆時比特幣可能下探 4.2 萬至 4.4 萬美元，較目前幣價約 6 萬美元仍有 30% 的下跌空間。
江卓爾的預測並非完全基於比特幣本身的技術線型，而是結合 Strategy 的市場估值，以及比特幣 4 年週期模型所推導出的結果。
江卓爾在社群平台 X 發文表示，目前 Strategy 的 mNAV（Market Net Asset Value，市值淨資產價值倍數）已跌至 0.72 。
所謂 mNAV，是指 Strategy 股價與每股持有比特幣價值的比值。當數值高於 1，代表市場願意給予 Strategy 高於其比特幣資產價值的溢價；若低於 1，則代表市場情緒偏向悲觀，認為公司估值甚至低於其持有的比特幣價值。
江卓爾指出，Strategy 目前 0.72 的 mNAV，已非常接近上一輪牛熊轉折時的低點。
對照上一輪熊市，mNAV 領先比特幣觸底約半年
他回顧指出，上一輪熊市中，Strategy 的 mNAV 曾於 2022 年 5 月 11 日跌至約 0.7，當時比特幣價格約 31,017 美元。
然而，比特幣真正的熊市低點並未同步出現，而是在約 6 個月後、也就是 2022 年 11 月 21 日才跌至 15,476 美元，當時 Strategy 的 mNAV 已回升至約 1.2 。
因此，江卓爾認為，mNAV 往往較比特幣價格更早觸底。若這項規律延續，本輪 mNAV 若已接近低點，則比特幣真正的價格底部，可能還需等待約半年時間。
除了觀察 Strategy 的估值變化，江卓爾也引用「比特幣 4 年週期模型」作為另一項依據。
他將比特幣的價格走勢比喻成「皮球落地反彈」，隨著比特幣市值不斷膨脹，它每次彈跳的幅度（即價格波動率）也會逐漸收斂縮小。
根據模型推算，比特幣本輪熊市低點將落在 2026 年 10 月 31 日 左右，對應價格約 44,016 美元。
不過，江卓爾也強調，這套模型對時間點的預測準確度，高於價格本身。因此，他綜合 mNAV 與 4 年週期模型後，認為本輪比特幣熊市將在 2026 年 10 月至 12 月觸底，價格介於 4.2 萬至 4.4 萬美元之間。
江卓爾認為，目前市場情緒已進入本輪週期最悲觀的階段，因此 Strategy 的估值可能率先觸底。基於這項判斷，他提出可考慮採取「做多 Strategy 、做空比特幣」的長期套利策略，等待兩者估值差距修復。
他也透露，自己近期的中短線操作策略一直是賣出現貨做空。不過，他表示，一旦市場進入預估的熊市底部區間，將開始重新買進比特幣現貨，轉為長線做多。
江卓爾的預測，也呼應近期市場偏空的悲觀氛圍。外匯經紀商 FxPro 日前指出，比特幣目前正測試 200 周移動平均線，從歷史經驗來看，一旦比特幣跌破此均線，往往都會伴隨長時間的弱勢整理。 FxPro 認為，5.5 萬美元很可能是比特幣下一個合理的低點。
另一方面，隨著美國聯準會（Fed）近期立場轉趨鷹派，市場原本因貨幣貶值預期而推升黃金、白銀及比特幣同步走高的交易邏輯，也正逐漸降溫，進一步加劇風險資產的修正壓力。

SBI 斥 2.8 億美元收購 Bitbank！登頂日本最大加密貨幣交易所
交易完成後，SBI 將整合旗下既有加密貨幣業務與 Bitbank 的資源，進一步搶攻穩定幣、數位資產金融服務市場，並有望成為日本資產管理規模最大的加密貨幣交易平台。
日本金融巨頭 SBI 控股（SBI Holdings）周四宣布，已正式簽署協議，將斥資 467 億日圓（約 2.88 億美元）收購日本加密貨幣交易所 Bitbank 。交易完成後，SBI 將整合旗下既有加密貨幣業務與 Bitbank 的資源，進一步搶攻穩定幣、數位資產金融服務市場，並有望成為日本資產管理規模最大的加密貨幣交易平台。
，這樁備受矚目的交易將透過 SBI 旗下全資子公司 SBICAH LLC 執行。交割程序完成後，Bitbank 將成為 SBI 間接控股的全資子公司，所有表決權也將由 SBI 全數掌握。
不過，這樁收購案仍須取得日本公平交易委員會（Japan Fair Trade Commission）的企業合併審查批准，並滿足其他交割條件。若一切進展順利，預計將於今年 10 月完成交割。
SBI 表示，完成併購後，將整合 Bitbank 加密貨幣業務的客戶基礎、服務開發能力、資安與法遵系統，以及管理資源，希望進一步擴大加密貨幣交易服務，同時開發穩定幣及其他數位資產相關的新金融產品。
據 SBI 估算，截至 2026 年 4 月底，集團旗下加密貨幣交易所 SBI VC Trade 與 Bitbank 合計管理的客戶加密資產規模達約 1.1 兆日圓（約 68 億美元），加密貨幣帳戶數則有 292 萬戶。
SBI 在聲明中表示，這將使集團成為日本管理資產規模最大的加密貨幣交易業者，帳戶數量亦位居頂尖之列。
根據公司資料，自成立以來，Bitbank 至今未曾發生任何駭客入侵事件，在安全性方面建立了良好的市場口碑。
事實上，SBI 早在今年 5 月就已對外證實，正與 Bitbank 洽談收購事宜，如今雙方正式簽署協議，也象徵這筆交易邁入最後階段。

https://blockcast.it/2026/06/26/multicoi.full_text:
上漲空間超過 400%！Multicoin 預測：HYPE 代幣 2028 年上看 319 美元
加密貨幣創投 Multicoin Capital 認為，隨著 Hyperliquid 從去中心化交易所進化為「全能交易所」，HYPE  到 2028 年有望飆升至 319 美元，較目前價格仍有逾 400% 的上漲空間。
加密貨幣創投 Multicoin Capital 發布重磅看多報告，直指市場嚴重低估 Hyperliquid 的原生代幣 HYPE 。該機構認為，隨著 Hyperliquid 從去中心化交易所，進化為「萬物皆可交易」的「全能交易所」，HYPE  到 2028 年有望飆升至 319 美元，較目前價格仍有逾 400% 的上漲空間。
Multicoin 周四發布研究報告指出，目前 HYPE 約 63 美元的價格，未能充分反映 Hyperliquid 未來的成長潛力。報告表示：
目前 HYPE 徘徊在 63 美元附近，我們認為市場完全給錯了定價，大家都只把 Hyperliquid 視為一家成長快速的去中心化永續合約交易所，視野過於狹隘了。
Multicoin 預估，在基本情境下，HYPE 到 2028 年可望創造約 80 億美元的年獲利。若以「20 倍本益比（P/E Ratio）」計算，HYPE 合理價位應落在 319 美元。
報告更揭露，自今年 2 月以來，Multicoin 一直在市場上瘋狂掃貨：「HYPE 現在已經是我們流動性避險基金中，規模最大的核心持倉之一。」
受一連串利多消息激勵，包含新上市 ETF 強勢吸金、營收表現亮眼，以及官方祭出積極的代幣回購計畫，HYPE 近期改寫歷史新高，一度突破 76 美元。
Multicoin 認為，Hyperliquid 已不再只是永續合約交易平台，而是逐步發展為更完整的鏈上金融基礎設施。其中最具代表性的案例，就是近期推出的 HIP-3 代幣化股票永續合約市場，在 SpaceX 上市首日就處理了 14 億美元的交易量，約占當日所有 HIP-3 交易量的 30% 。
Multicoin 指出，回顧整個 2025 年，Hyperliquid 的用戶數從約 30 萬人呈爆發式增長至 92.3 萬人；未平倉量更狂翻 3 倍，從 20 億美元飆升至 60 億美元。
報告進一步披露，Hyperliquid 去年累計創造約 8.73 億美元的驚人營收，全年交易量高達 2.9 兆美元，穩坐全球最大去中心化衍生品交易所的寶座，更是目前全球成長最快的金融應用程式之一。
「我們預估的 319 美元基本目標價，其實還顯得保守，」Multicoin 點出，目前模型尚未納入多項潛在催化因素，包括：即將問世的 HIP-4 升級、 HyperEVM，以及投資組合保證金功能上線後對旗艦產品所帶來的綜效。
為了強化自身預測的可信度，Multicoin 也回顧過去的成功投資案例。報告提到，公司早在 2019 年、 BNB 約 10 美元時就曾公開喊多，而如今 BNB 已突破 550 美元。此外，Multicoin 也是 Solana 生態早期最重要的支持者之一。

https://blockcast.it/2026/06/26/ark-inve.full_text:
趁大跌掃貨！「女股神」加碼買進 Coinbase 、 Circle 等 4 檔加密概念股
就在股、幣市全面下殺之際，由「女股神」Cathie Wood 掌舵的方舟投資（ARK Invest）趁勢進場逢低承接，大舉掃入 Coinbase、Circle、Bullish 以及 Robinhood 等加密貨幣概念股，持續展現對加密產業長期成長前景的信心。
就在股、幣市全面下殺，投資人縮手之際，由「女股神」Cathie Wood 掌舵的方舟投資（ARK Invest）趁勢進場逢低承接，大舉掃入 Coinbase 、 Circle 、 Bullish 以及 Robinhood 等加密貨幣概念股，持續展現對加密產業長期成長前景的信心。同時，Cathie Wood 也重申，她認為通膨正持續降溫，未來貨幣政策的走向可能比市場預期更為寬鬆。
根據最新揭露的交易數據顯示，方舟投資透過旗下 3 檔主動式 ETF ：ARKK 、 ARKW 與 ARKF，一口氣買進了 9,014 股 Coinbase 。若以周四的收盤價計算，這筆加碼規模約達 128 萬美元。
除了 Coinbase，方舟還同步買進了 9,264 股的 Circle 股票，以及 9,136 股的加密貨幣機構級交易所 Bullish 。此外，方舟更透過旗艦基金 ARKK，斥資約 327 萬美元，買進 35,023 股 Robinhood 股票。
值得注意的是，方舟投資這波「逆勢加碼」的時機，正值這 4 檔股票全面下挫之際。 Coinbase 股價周四下跌 5% 至 142.52 美元；Circle 下跌 3% 來到 68.81 美元；Robinhood 下滑 3.85% 收在 93.47 美元；而 Bullish 更是重挫 6.77%，跌至 21.88 美元。
方舟投資一向積極動態調整旗下 ETF 的持股權重，並嚴守「單一個股權畢重不得超過基金總規模 10%」的鐵律。這意味著，當某些資產的價格出現劇烈波動時，方舟就會啟動「再平衡」機制，藉由買進跌深的股票來維持權重比例。
針對市場近期的動盪與焦慮，Cathie Wood 也在社群平台 X 上發表長文，直指通膨其實正在降溫的路上，並強調「生產力提升」正是壓抑物價的核心力量。
：「最近我在亞洲與歐洲進行海外法說會時，深深感受到投資人對通膨的恐懼。當我告訴他們，通膨很可能會出現大幅度的回落，而且這不僅僅是因為油價下跌而已，他們都感到相當訝異。」她進一步以數據佐證自己的觀點：
若從「單位勞動成本（Unit Labor Costs，衡量企業生產每單位產品所需支付的勞工薪資成本）」來看，年增率已經降至 0.5% 。
我相信，聯準會（Fed）新任主席華許（Kevin Warsh）不僅清楚生產力在抗通膨中所扮演的關鍵角色，更看透了官方通膨數據背後的盲點與缺陷。
面對華爾街近期一片「準備迎接更高利率」的聲浪，Cathie Wood 評論稱：「儘管現在市場上許多人預期，升息的腳步會比幾個月前來得更快，但我深信，華許將會為整個金融市場，上一堂大師級的貨幣政策課。」

又爆當機災情！Base 出塊中斷、交易暫停  2 小時
由 Coinbase 孵化的以太坊 Layer 2 網路「 Base 」周四驚傳當機災情，區塊生產中斷近 2 小時，所幸經緊急搶修後，目前已順利恢復出塊，但事故原因仍在調查中。
由 Coinbase 孵化的以太坊 Layer 2 網路「Base」周四驚傳當機災情，區塊生產中斷近 2 小時，所幸經緊急搶修後，目前已順利恢復出塊，但事故原因仍在調查中。
，目前 Base 已重啟運行，內部節點亦恢復正常的數據同步。不過，團隊至今仍在調查當機原因，並建議節點營運商重新啟動 Base 節點，以恢復同步狀態。
原事發經過，Base 在世界協調時間（UTC）下午 4 點 03 分首次對外通報主網的出塊狀態「不正常」。不到一小時，團隊於下午 4 點 52 分證實已鎖定問題癥結點，並迅速展開搶修。

作為以太坊生態系中規模數一數二的 Layer 2 ，這次當機一度導致 Base 鏈上的所有交易處理被迫全面中斷，引起社群高度關注。截至目前，Base 尚未對外公布「無效區塊」產生的原因，也未說明事故是否源自軟體漏洞，或是因共識機制相關的故障所致。
值得注意的是，Base 原本就預計在事發當天的 UTC 時間下午 6 點，進行名為「Beryl」的重大升級，不過就目前官方披露的資訊看來，這起當機事件與排定好的升級似乎並無直接關聯。
根據 The Block 數據，Base 目前是交投最熱絡、最活躍的以太坊擴容解決方案。然而，這並非 Base 首次面臨大規模停機的技術考驗，該網路去年 8 月也曾爆發過類似的當機災情。
針對這次風波，Base 團隊承諾將持續嚴密監控網路的穩定性，並隨著調查的深入，隨時向市場更新最新進展。

比特幣急殺跌破 5.8 萬美元！數據：「軋空行情」醞釀中、空軍恐遭狙擊
周四美股開盤之際，比特幣無預警上演大跳水，急殺 5% 跌破 5.8 萬美元大關，寫下 2024 年以來的最低紀錄。不過，儘管現貨市場賣壓沉重，衍生品市場卻開始浮現回補壓力，軋空行情可期。
周四美股開盤之際，比特幣無預警上演大跳水，急殺 5% 跌破 5.8 萬美元大關，寫下 2024 年以來的最低紀錄。不過，儘管現貨市場賣壓沉重，衍生品市場卻開始浮現回補壓力，軋空行情可期。
，比特幣目前仍在 58,800 美元附近徘徊，過去 24 小時下跌 3%，這波拋售潮也迅速蔓延至整體加密貨幣市場：以太幣下跌 5.7%，滑落至 1,530 美元左右；而瑞波幣（XRP）、 Solana（SOL）也難逃一劫，分別下跌 4.7% 、 1% 。
資金面來看，市場正呈現兩極化的走勢。儘管記憶體大廠美光（Micron）在周三盤後繳出亮眼財報，帶動股價狂飆，但多數科技巨頭股價卻普遍走跌，最終拖累那斯達克指數收黑 0.4%，避險情緒也連帶波及了加密貨幣市場。
，更緊盯聯準會（Fed）動向。在新任主席華許（Kevin Warsh）的帶領下，Fed 上周意外展現極度「鷹派」的姿態。決策官員甚至暗示，下一步幾乎篤定是升息而非降息，且升息的時間點恐將比華爾街原先預期的還要早得多，這無疑讓風險資產承壓。
儘管比特幣仍處於去年 10 月以來的下跌趨勢，但若從衍生品市場的數據來剖析，短期內或許有望迎來喘息空間。
」，可以發現大量的清算風險密集分布在目前幣價的「上方」，而非「下方」。這意味著，即便比特幣繼續下探，也不太容易引發「連環斷頭（強制平倉）」賣壓；相反，現在真正身處險境的，反而是那些重倉做空的投資人。
此外，儘管比特幣下跌約 3%，過去 24 小時內的「未平倉合約（Open Interest）」卻逆勢增加 0.28%，代表交易員並未因下跌而平倉，反而持續建立新的空單，押注比特幣將跌破 5.8 萬美元的重要支撐。
同時，目前市場的「資金費率（Funding Rates）」仍維持負值，意味著投資人願意支付額外成本持續持有空頭部位，也反映市場對進一步下跌的預期仍相當濃厚。
（Market Depth，衡量市場吸收大額交易而不影響價格的能力）」卻暗藏撐盤力道。
根據 CoinGlass 統計，從目前幣價一路往下至 50,000 美元區間，訂單簿上總計有高達 6,900 枚比特幣（價值約 4.09 億美元）的買單；相較之下，從現價到 70,000 美元之間的賣單卻僅有 1,570 枚比特幣。這種籌碼供需的不對稱，形成了有利於多頭的底部支撐。
在華爾街與幣圈的歷史經驗中，當市場出現這種極度「擁擠」的一面倒交易時，敏銳的操盤手與造市商往往會精準狙擊這個弱點，逆勢拉抬價格。
一旦反撲的號角響起，原先做空的投資人為了避免持續支付高昂的資金費率，甚至為了防範遭到清算斷頭，將被迫買回比特幣平倉，這股反向買盤很可能會點燃「軋空行情」，推升比特幣迎來一波快速反彈。

Meta 25 日發表全新 Meta Glasses 系列智慧眼鏡，首度以自有品牌名稱推出，告別過去四年與 Ray-Ban 的合作模式。這次發表不僅代表 Meta 穿戴裝置策略的重大轉型，更因網紅兼商業大亨 Kylie Jenner 聯名款引爆網路熱議，讓「時尚科技」與「隱私監控」的爭論再度浮上檯面。
Meta Glasses 系列共推出三款造型：適合日常穿搭的 Wayfarer 風格 Meta Adventure、外型粗獷前衛的 Meta Fury，以及與 Kylie Jenner 聯名打造的高端款 Starfire Kylie Edition。三款售價從 299 美元起跳，共有 26 種顏色與鏡片組合選擇。
Starfire Kylie Edition 定價 399 美元，若選配漸變灰變色鏡片（Transitions）版本為 479 美元。外觀為輕薄橢圓形太陽眼鏡，更像精品配件而非科技產品，這正是 Meta 的設計初衷。聯名款內建寶石點綴、鏡面充電盒、可調節鼻托，以及 Jenner 的專屬語音選項，喚醒功能音效甚至沿用她走紅的招牌台詞「rise and shine」。
硬體方面，Meta Glasses 搭載 1,200 萬畫素鏡頭，可拍攝 3K 影片，並配備開放式揚聲器與六麥克風陣列，單次使用電力可達 8 小時，搭配充電盒總續航力延伸至 48 小時。眼鏡同時支援處方鏡片替換計畫。
AI 功能由 Meta 自行研發的 Spark 模型驅動，是 Meta Glasses 有別於前代 Ray-Ban 合作款的最大升級。Spark 可即時理解周遭環境、提供情境建議與任務提醒，不依賴擴增實境顯示器，操作更直覺、介入感更低。
分析人士指出，Meta 是刻意擺脫「借來的品牌光環」。雖然 Ray-Ban 經典輪廓幫助過 Meta 讓智慧眼鏡更親民，但 AI 穿戴裝置逐漸成為獨立品類，Meta 顯然認為是時候讓自己的名字站上舞台。此次改以 Kylie Jenner 當成行銷賣點，瞄準另一種形式的品牌信賴感：消費文化的話語權。
新品發表後網路反應卻十分兩極。支持者認為 Meta 找對了人：有人在社群媒體直言「矽谷終於搞清楚誰掌控消費市場了」，另有人稱讚眼鏡外觀時尚、行銷聲勢驚人。也有人與 Snap 同期發表、定價高達 2,195 美元的 Specs AR 眼鏡相比，突顯 Meta 掌握行銷流量方面的優勢。
然而，更多聲音指向隱私疑慮。智慧眼鏡內建鏡頭讓部分用戶感到不安，與拿手機錄影相比，戴著外觀時髦的眼鏡悄悄側錄，旁人幾乎無從察覺。討論串裡有人提到健身房、酒吧、學校等場所可能淪為隱性攝影地帶；一名用戶直言「我健身房有人天天戴著 Meta 眼鏡，每次看到都覺得毛毛的」。
而 Meta 強調已設計可視錄影指示燈與防竄改偵測機制，力求兼顧透明度與用戶信任。
Meta Glasses 系列在 Meta 官網及 Best Buy、亞馬遜、Sunglass Hut、LensCrafters 等美國主要零售通路開賣。競爭對手動輒數千美元的 AR 眼鏡，Meta 以 299 美元起價搶攻大眾市場，試圖將 AI 穿戴裝置從小眾極客玩具，轉化為人人負擔得起的日常配件。
而 Kylie Jenner 加持下，新眼鏡當然成功躋身話題中心。然而，當時尚與監控科技的邊界愈來愈模糊，這場圍繞 AI 眼鏡的論戰，才正要開始。

微軟（Microsoft Corp.）宣布，由於儲存與記憶體價格一口氣翻了超過 2.5 倍，決定調漲 Xbox Series S 遊戲主機售價。
綜合CNBC、MarketWatch報導，根據微軟旗下Xbox部門25日
的官方部落格，自8月1日起，自8月1日起，配備512GB儲存空間的Xbox機型售價調漲100美元、來到約500美元；配備1TB儲存空間的Xbox售價調漲150美元；入門款的Xbox售價如今則為750美元起。另一方面，配備2TB儲存空間的Xbox主機則將正式停產。
微軟透過部落格表示，「去年10月，我們才將美國市場的Xbox主機售價調高20~70美元。我們原本希望不需要再次漲價，過去幾月也持續跟供應商討論各種替代方案，但顯然事與願違。」
微軟指出，「主機的儲存空間與記憶體價格已暴漲超過2.5倍，且預期到2027年秋季，價格還會再翻倍。」
蘋果（Apple Inc.）25日稍早宣布調漲MacBook、iPad售價前，執行長庫克（Tim Cook）接受《華爾街日報》採訪時就曾直言，調高售價「無可避免」。
值得注意的是，微軟在文章中透露，「遊戲主機在定價時通常不是以獲利為導向，而是以『低於製造成本』的虧本模式在販售。」
微軟25日聞訊下挫3.45%、收352.83美元，創2023年11月3日以來收盤新低；年初迄今跌幅已多達27.04%。
Xbox事業部新任執行長Asha Sharma 6月10日就在官方部落格上表示，Xbox在2月支付的儲存成本已是2025年秋天的2倍，且此後價格再度翻倍。到了2027年，預估儲存成本將是2025年的五倍以上。記憶體成本的軌跡也大致相似。
文章指出，雖然整個業界都受到這場零組件危機的衝擊，但Xbox由於「過去五年所做的選擇」，受到的打擊尤為沉重。如此嚴峻局面使得微軟生產的遊戲機數量難以滿足玩家需求，進而迫使團隊開始考慮「全新的硬體商業模式與夥伴關係」。
文章並稱，Xbox部門過去五年雖然對內容、平台與硬體補貼投入超過200億美元，同期間年營收卻萎縮5億美元。「這種情況不能再持續下去。」

知名爆料人士 Evan Blass 今日公開疑似三星 Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 官方宣傳圖，讓這款尚未發表的高階智慧手錶提前曝光。從流出圖片看來，新機延續前代偏方圓（squircle）錶身輪廓，並有黑色與綠色兩種；整體外觀雖然變化不大，但細節仍可看出有改動。
圖片顯示，Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 錶圈改以數字刻度取代線條標示；錶背標示 47mm、藍寶石玻璃（sapphire crystal）、LTE 與 GPS，以及 10ATM 防水等級。右側可見三星慣用的三鍵設計，中央為圓形主按鈕，側邊按鍵區域據報將獲得改良，錶圈也可能較前代更薄，但外觀變動幅度不大且難從圖片判斷。

Google 尚未上市的 Home Speaker 在美國某家沃爾瑪（Walmart）被消費者提前購得並分享實測心得，引發討論。這款定價 99 美元的智慧喇叭整體表現獲正面評價，中低頻表現與音量令人滿意，設定流程也相當快速；但固定式電源線（captive cable）成為最大爭議點。
網友 rrelevantIronman 在 Reddit
，他在沃爾瑪架上發現並買下這款官方還未正式出貨的產品。實測顯示，喇叭音質比預期好，聽完一套高階音響系統測試後仍有相當水準。介面設計簡潔，頂端網布下有隱藏燈光顯示音量，並可敲擊操作；設定也很容易，用 Google Home 帳號並以行動熱點連線，10 分鐘內就能設好。
最大爭議在電源線無法拆換：線材直接固定於機身，長度不到 5 英尺，與 Google 舊款可拆換線材不同，若未來電源線損壞，使用者自行更換相對困難，可能需拆機或交由專業維修人員處理。
且 Google 也未隱瞞這點。Google Store 規格頁面，包裝內附 30W USB-C 變壓器，明確標示「captive cable」。整體而言，若不考慮固定電源線這點，此 99 美元的 Home Speaker 體積與價格很有機會成為非蘋用戶尋找 HomePod mini 替代品的選項。

國際宣布引進 DJI 新款口袋型攝影機 Osmo Pocket 4P，預計 6 月 29 日在台上市。此一新品鎖定專業影像創作者、Vlogger、短影音創作者，以及有進階拍攝需求的使用者。
隨著 Vlog、短影音與行動影像創作需求持續成長，口袋型攝影設備逐漸成為手機之外的第二台拍攝工具。DJI 今年 4 月推出 Osmo Pocket 4 後，再推出定位更高階的 Osmo Pocket 4P，主打雙主攝、光學變焦與更高動態範圍，補足專業創作者在攜帶性與影像品質之間的需求。
聯強國際資訊事業部總經理林意峰表示，Pocket 4 上市後，短時間內銷售表現優於預期，一個月內累積銷售突破萬台；此次引進 Pocket 4P，則是希望進一步切入更高階的影像創作市場，滿足商業拍攝、活動紀錄、街拍、運動追焦等多元應用。
Osmo Pocket 4P 採雙鏡頭設計，分別搭載 1 英吋廣角鏡頭與 1/1.28 英吋中焦鏡頭，支援 3 倍光學變焦、6 倍無損變焦，最高可達 12 倍數位變焦。相較前代產品，新機更強調遠距構圖、人像拍攝與背景虛化效果，讓使用者在不同拍攝場景中，能以單機完成更多鏡位需求。
影像能力部分，Osmo Pocket 4P 的 1 英吋廣角鏡頭導入 LOFIC 技術，標榜可達 17 檔動態範圍，並支援 D-Log 2 色彩模式，提供後期調色彈性；此外，新機也支援 4K 240fps 超級慢動作拍攝，適合運動、活動紀錄或需要慢動作效果的創作場景。
DJI Pocket 系列自 2018 年問世以來，主打小型化機身、三軸雲台穩定與行動拍攝體驗。此次 Osmo Pocket 4P 延續口袋型機身設計，並導入 DJI 圖傳技術，可透過取景遙控器進行即時影像傳輸與遠端操作，提升多人拍攝、固定機位或活動紀錄時的操作彈性。搭配 DJI Mic 等周邊設備直連，也有助於強化收音與影像工作流程。
隨著 Osmo Pocket 4P 加入，DJI Osmo Pocket 產品線也更完整。聯強表示，萬元價位帶的 Pocket 3 仍鎖定一般大眾與入門使用者；1.5 萬元級距的 Pocket 4 則主打日常創作與進階拍攝需求；新款 Pocket 4P 則上探高階影像市場，訴求以約 2 萬元價位帶提供更接近專業攝影設備的影像表現。
聯強指出，Osmo Pocket 4P 詳細建議售價與通路活動，將於 6 月 29 日晚間 8 時正式公告。

Tether putting $23 billion gold stockpile to work with bullion-backed loans
The stablecoin issuer is extending its tokenized gold strategy by allowing holders of XAUT to borrow against their bullion, mirroring bitcoin-backed lending without selling the underlying asset.
Jun 27, 2026, 3:00 p.m.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino (Nikhilesh De/CoinDesk)
Tether and Ledn are expected to offer gold-backed loans later this year.
The move extends the utility of Tether's $23 billion gold reserve allowing holders to borrow against tokenized gold rather than selling it.
The offering mirrors Ledn's bitcoin-backed lending model.
Tether has expanded the use of its $23 billion gold reserves by bringing its tokenized product Tether Gold (XAUT) to crypto lender Ledn.
Ledn said it is adding support for XAUT, alongside bitcoin
and Tether's stablecoin USDT, with
borrowing against XAUT expected later this year
Tether is attempting to monetize what has become one of the world's largely privately held gold reserves. The stablecoin company says it holds around $23 billion worth of physical bullion backing XAUT, with each token representing one troy ounce of gold stored in vaults in Switzerland.
Gold-backed lending is traditionally the realm of central banks, major financial institutions and bullion dealers. Tether and Ledn argue that by tokenizing physical gold, the asset can function more like physical bitcoin as digital collateral, unlocking liquidity without having to sell it.
This follows the model Ledn has used for bitcoin-backed loans for several years. Client collateral continues to be held 1:1, without being lent out or used to generate yield, Ledn said, seeking to draw a line between the services it offers and those of its
former rivals that went to the wall in the crypto winter of 2022
"As digital assets become an increasingly important part of the global economy, demand is growing for solutions that combine long-term ownership with financial flexibility," Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said in a statement.
The move is the latest example of Tether leveraging the profits generated by USDT, the world's largest stablecoin, to expand beyond its core business. The company has spent the past few years reshaping itself into a broader technology and infrastructure group spanning finance, energy and AI.
A key part of that strategy has been building a substantial gold business. Alongside growing XAUT, Tether has accumulated roughly 140 metric tons of physical bullion, making it one of the world's largest corporate gold holders. It has also invested in
precious metals marketplace Gold.com
partnered with crypto financing firm Antalpha
to expand the use of XAUT in lending and physical redemption.
Beyond precious metals, Tether has
invested in bitcoin mining
renewable energy projects
AI infrastructure provider Northern Data
and as part of a broader push into computing technologies.

Coinbase and OKX try to lure in Binance’s EU users after it failed to secure a MiCA license
Brian Armstrong of Coinbase and Star Xu of OKX offered new users sign up bonuses of up to 8% of their deposits or transfers from other accounts.
Jun 27, 2026, 2:20 p.m.
Jun 27, 2026, 2:11 p.m.
Coinbase CEO and Founder Brian Armstrong offered new users in the EU sign up bonuses a day after Binance told its clients it will suspend certain crypto services from July 1. (Jesse Hamilton/CoinDesk)
Coinbase and OKX moved quickly to court Binance’s European users after Binance said it would suspend some services in the European Union because it lacks a MiCA license by the July 1 deadline.
Coinbase, which says it has been MiCA-licensed since 2025, is offering a 5 percent transfer bonus to new users in several major European markets and the U.K. who move funds to the platform before July 13.
OKX is pitching itself as a long-term regulated alternative in Europe with one of its largest welcome campaigns, including bonuses and deposit matching of up to 8 percent for eligible users in the European Economic Area, as Binance works to secure a MiCA license after withdrawing its Greek application.
Coinbase and OKX are offering sign-up bonuses to users after reports broke out that rival exchange Binance
in the European Union (EU) it is suspending some services because it will not have a Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) license in place by July 1.
Brian Armstrong, CEO and founder of Coinbase,
wrote on X Friday evening offering users
in Germany, France, Italy, Belgium, Poland, Sweden and the U.K. sign up bonuses. He
pointed to his firm’s website
where the offers were explained in more detail.
“Coinbase has been MiCA licensed since 2025 and offers unified global liquidity across spot and derivatives,” the crypto exchange says in its offer to new users.
“We’re offering a 5% transfer bonus for people moving funds to Coinbase before July 13th,” it adds.
Star Xu, OKX founder and CEO, also offered bonuses to new users in Europe i
n an X post on Saturday
saying that MiCA marks the start of a new era for crypto in the region.
“If you’re looking for a regulated platform built for the long term, we’re excited to welcome you to OKX,” he said. “To celebrate this new chapter, we’re offering one of our biggest welcome campaigns for eligible EEA users, including welcome bonuses and deposit matching of up to 8%.”
Binance emailed its users notifying them the exchange was no longer able to accept new registrations and would restrict services, a spokesperson for the Abu Dhabi-based company told CoinDesk. "Your assets remain safe and secure, and will remain accessible at all times," the email said.
On Thursday, the company said it
withdrew its license application
in Greece and would seek authorization in another EU country.
However, in a statement to CoinDesk, Binance said its "ambitions in Europe remain the same, and we are confident we will secure a MiCA licence in the coming months."
The emails to clients in France, Italy, Poland and Spain come days before a June 30 deadline. Crypto firms must have a MiCA license from at least one EU member state by July 1 to provide services across all 27 member states. Unlicensed firms must wind down their EU activities.

Conno Christou doesn’t leave things to chance. He tracks his sleep with a Whoop band, cross-references it with an Oura ring, and gets nearly 100 biomarkers checked every year. He had been doing the annual bloodwork for four consecutive years, following the protocols of longevity researchers like Peter Attia and Rhonda Patrick. He was optimizing his supplements, his circadian rhythm, his protein intake.
At 35, building his second company, he was as dialed-in on the latest in health research as anyone he knew. His last checkup, in 2025, was green across the board. “It was the best I’d had in years,” he says.
Then, after a workout, his arm swelled.
He didn’t think much of it at first. A week passed before he saw a doctor, who found two blood clots in his veins and scheduled surgery. But the pre-op exams changed everything. A doctor walked back into the room and told him the procedure wasn’t happening.
“We see an 11-by-11-by-8 centimeter mass behind your sternum,” the doctor said.
A biopsy confirmed what Christou had never before even contemplated. He had an aggressive, fast-growing form of non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma — a rare diagnosis affecting roughly one in 420,000 people, caused by a random genetic mutation with no connection to lifestyle, diet, or stress.
The tumor had only existed for about three months. In three more weeks, it would have reached stage four.
“Lucky in my unluckiness,” Christou told this editor this week from his home in Athens, where he lives part time. “It was only found because I went in for something else entirely.”
What followed was an education in the limits of the medical system, and in what a determined patient can do about that with tools now available.
His first oncologist, a renowned specialist, recommended the lighter of two available chemotherapy regimens. Christou booked his first infusion three days out. Then, the night before, he sought a second opinion.
That second doctor didn’t hesitate. He recommended the harder regimen — continuous in-hospital infusion, cycling every three weeks across six months — citing Christou’s specific pathology. The lighter treatment carried roughly a 60% success rate for his presentation. The aggressive one brought that number to around 85%. Two world-class doctors. Diametrically opposite recommendations.
“As founders, we hold the wheel,” Christou says of the propensity of many people to accept what they are told —  and why more should not. “You hear many things. You don’t have to follow the first advice.”
He didn’t opt to just follow the advice of the second physician, either. Over the next two days, he gathered 12 opinions in total — drawing on his professional network, reaching out to hematologists and oncologists in the US and abroad, calling in every favor he could. Eleven to one voted in favor of the harder path. He took it. The decision, he says, didn’t feel brave so much as logical. He was already a data-driven person, and now the stakes felt existential to him.
Over six months of treatment, Christou approached chemotherapy the way he approached building a company, as a marathon of sprints — each of them with a finite cycle and each week filled with data points. He had done a mandatory 25-month military service in Cyprus at age 18 and he borrowed from that experience, too. He was going to be a good soldier, he told himself. Trust the process. Six cycles. Get through it.
He wore his Whoop throughout, and found it remarkably accurate at predicting the days his immune system would bottom out, sometimes flagging them before symptoms arrived. He kept a symptom journal using voice transcription, logging every shift, every side effect, every medication and counter-medication. He narrowed his focus to three variables: sleep, nutrition, and, first and foremost, psychology. (“It moves the needle more than anything,” said Christou. “I never asked ‘why me’ — not once. That question has no useful answer.”)
He fed all of it — blood results, scan data, wearable output, journal entries — into Claude. He’s far from alone in turning to chatbots for medical guidance. A
released in March found that a third of American adults now use them for health information and advice. The
accumulating online suggest that for some patients, AI is delivering what the system couldn’t.
Experts urge caution; Danielle Bitterman, clinical lead for data science and AI at Mass General Brigham, has told the New York Times in recent months that general-purpose chatbots are
and “have not been thoroughly evaluated” for personalized diagnoses.
Christou doesn’t disagree. “It didn’t replace the doctors,” he says, but it “helped me ask the right questions.”
For a condition as rare as his — one an oncologist might see once a year — access to a model that had absorbed the full body of medical literature was, he says, simply not the same as a Google search.
The model proved critical at the end of treatment. His final PET scan — the imaging used to detect active disease — came back ambiguous. His oncologist began discussing a second line of therapy, potentially radiotherapy, near his heart and lungs. It was an alarming development.
Christou again did his homework. He read that for this specific lymphoma, the false-positive rate on end-of-treatment PET scans is around 60% — a statistic that still astonishes him. “It’s 2026,” he says. “Sixty percent.”
He fed all three of his PET scans and his MRI into Claude, which flagged a known but easily overlooked phenomenon: in patients under 40 recovering from this type of lymphoma, the thymus gland can reactivate after chemotherapy, showing up on imaging as what appears to be active disease. Given his age, his specific scan characteristics, the model put the probability of that explanation at roughly 90%.
He sought three more opinions. The fourth doctor confirmed it: thymus rebound. There was no active disease. No radiotherapy was needed. He was clear.
Christou is still unfolding what the last year has meant, for his health, how he works, and how he thinks about time. He built Keragon, his current company, before any of this happened; it’s an AI-powered platform that helps medical practices automate their administrative operations.
But going through the system as a patient has given him new perspective. He watched nurses and doctors buried under tasks that had nothing to do with care. He received the same chemotherapy protocol as an 80-year-old woman, the side effects managed through a cascading chain of additional drugs, each causing problems of their own. He says he’s certain that we will look back at this era of treatment and cringe.
He takes Sundays off now, mostly. He tries to be present — at lunch with friends, at home with his dog, in conversations that might once have felt like a distraction from work. A VC friend told him something years ago that he said he kept replaying during treatment: Be happy now. He says it’s among the hardest things to do and yet he finally appreciates its importance.
He says he’d be happy to talk to anyone going through something similar to share notes, compare experiences. He seems to means it.
“It’s not happening in 10 years,” he says of what AI can already do for patients willing to use it. “It’s happening today.”

Why a selloff in gold and silver is dragging bitcoin down
Bitcoin has long been lumped in with precious metals as a hedge against a weakening dollar. That trade is unwinding on a hawkish Fed, and bitcoin is falling alongside the metals it was supposed to rival.
Jun 27, 2026, 6:11 p.m.
A broad unwinding of the so-called debasement trade is hitting gold, silver and bitcoin at once, as investors retreat from scarce assets once seen as protection against currency erosion.
A newly hawkish Federal Reserve under Chair Kevin Warsh and a stronger dollar are lifting real yields, making non-yielding assets like gold, silver and bitcoin less attractive and more expensive for foreign buyers.
Bitcoin, which lagged metals on the way up but is now closely tracking their decline, has fallen about 50 percent from its peak even as it has recently outperformed gold and silver on a relative basis, underscoring its dual role as both a speculative asset and a hard-money hedge.
The ongoing artificial intelligence stock frenzy has pulled in capital from across the market, from traditional metals, considered the safest assets, to crypto, considered the riskiest.
Gold dropped below $4,000 for the first time since November earlier this week, silver has lost more than half its value from its high, and bitcoin has slipped to nearly $58,000.
The three selloffs are not a coincidence. For much of the past two years, they have been, to a large degree, the same trade, and now the same forces are
That trade even has a name, the "debasement" trade. It is the bet that heavy government spending and rising national debt will slowly erode the value of paper money, which pushes investors toward scarce assets that no government can print more of.
Gold and silver are the oldest versions of that bet, while bitcoin, with a supply capped at 21 million coins, got marketed as the digital version. Through 2025, as the dollar looked vulnerable, money poured into all three, and they were treated as one basket.
What groups them on the way up also groups them on the way down. The new Federal Reserve chair, Kevin Warsh, struck a hawkish tone at his first meeting, and markets are now pricing two quarter-point rate hikes by March 2027, which would lift the Fed's benchmark rate to 4.00% to 4.25%. The U.S. dollar has climbed 0.8% this week alone.
Both of those work directly against hard assets. Higher rates lift real yields, the return on safe assets like Treasuries after accounting for inflation, which raises the cost of holding gold, silver or bitcoin, none of which pay any yield.
A stronger dollar makes all three more expensive for buyers using other currencies. So when gold and silver fall, it is usually a signal that the macro regime has turned against this narrative.
Bitcoin's place in the basket has always been awkward. Through most of 2025, as gold and silver rallied hard, bitcoin went sideways near $100,000. That divergence opened a question of whether it still belonged in the debasement trade at all, or whether its role as a hedge against currency dilution had faded.
But a rather uncomfortable occurrence now is that bitcoin lagged the metals on the way up, but is tracking them closely on the way down.
The scale of the reversal is large. Gold is down about 28% from its January 2025 record near $5,600, silver has fallen more than 50% from its high near $120, and bitcoin has dropped roughly 50% from its October peak. That move took bitcoin below its 200-week moving average, the average price over the past four years and a closely watched long-term floor, at about $60,000.
However, there is one bright spot for bitcoin holders, though it comes with a catch.
Since these ratios bottomed in February, bitcoin has actually outperformed both metals, gaining roughly 30% against gold and more than 55% against silver.
Bitcoin trades as two things at once, a speculative risk asset and a hard-money hedge, and right now, both readings point the same way. The debasement trade was the bull case that lifted it with gold and silver, but its unwind is the bear case pulling it back down with them.
As long as the Fed stays hawkish and the dollar stays firm, bitcoin will likely struggle to break away from the metals it has been compared to for years.

What Robinhood’s recent layoffs say about the current state of crypto investments
Despite the trading platform’s restructuring and the wave of crypto companies making cuts, signaling a late bear market, Altcoin Pro’s Horst, Anderson and Zhuleku explain there’s no reason to panic.
Jun 27, 2026, 4:30 p.m.
Bull and bear market (Midjourney/modified by CoinDesk)
Read the recent headlines about trading platform
Robinhood’s c-suite departure
BitGo’s 15% workforce reduction
, and you’ll see that things are looking grim in the world of crypto investing. One outlet reports that Robinhood's recent decision to reduce its headcount is occurring amid a “
crypto revenue crunch
.” Another called the current crypto season a “
For investors, understanding the correlation between tech layoffs and crypto market performance is valuable. In this case, the lesson to be learned is that Robinhood’s layoffs aren’t influencing the market, but revealing where we are in the market cycle.
Based on declining trading volumes, sector-wide cost-cutting, reduced venture funding, and subdued retail participation, eight months after Bitcoin topped, these signals point to a late bear market environment. That is not a reason to panic. In fact, late bear markets have historically been some of the best times to position for the next bull run.
Robinhood’s layoffs are an indicator of market sentiment
Crypto market movements are influenced by factors such as liquidity, interest rates, institutional adoption, regulation and overall market sentiment. Because these are the factors that drive movement, these are the things investors look at as they try to predict movement.
announced by Robinhood
in the middle of June 2026 generally fall under the category of market sentiment. They are a lagging indicator of declining or a lack of investor confidence.
During bull markets, crypto companies tend to hire aggressively as trading volume, funding and revenue grow. During bear markets, companies often cut costs and reduce headcount as activity slows down.
We’ve seen this pattern repeatedly across exchanges, market makers, venture funds and crypto startups. Weaker market conditions often lead to both lower crypto prices and more layoffs.
In the case of crypto, however, the depth of the slump can vary based on the asset. Larger assets like bitcoin and Ethereum tend to be the most resilient during market shifts because they have the deepest liquidity, the strongest institutional demand and the most established ecosystems. Smaller altcoins and speculative assets tend to be more sensitive to shifts in market sentiment because they rely more heavily on retail participation and risk appetite.
This is also why experienced investors often use periods of low volatility or market consolidation to focus on yield-generating strategies. Staking, DeFi and liquidity provision can help generate returns on assets already being held rather than relying solely on price appreciation. During sideways or early bear markets, these passive income strategies can be valuable tools for retail investors.
Robinhood traders could benefit from the recent layoffs
Those who have come to rely on Robinhood may worry that a significant reduction in staffing could leave them without the resources they need to trade. The reality, however, will more likely be a better experience.
The main thing to understand is that Robinhood’s trading platform doesn’t rely on hundreds of employees manually executing trades. Most of what handles that activity is automated infrastructure and software. The people being let go seem to be mostly management and support-related roles, not the engineers keeping the platform running.
One thing that’s often overlooked is that layoffs can actually strengthen a company’s financial position. By reducing payroll expenses, Robinhood improves its profit margins and lowers operating costs. Investors on Wall Street often view that favorably because it means the company can generate more profit from the same amount of revenue.
The biggest place users might notice a difference is customer support. If you run into an account issue, a transfer delay, or something that requires a real human to step in, response times may be slower for a while.
As for trading, deposits, withdrawals and normal investing activity, users shouldn’t expect much to change. If there are any bumps from the restructuring, they’re usually worked out within a few months as teams adjust.
Robinhood says layoffs aren’t being driven by AI integration
published on June 4, 2026, AI has been the top‌ reason cited for tech layoffs during 2026. Robinhood, however, seems to be taking a different tack.
BitGo, attributing its cuts to AI
, Robinhood hasn’t indicated these layoffs were driven by AI adoption. The company’s
is that it’s reducing management layers and streamlining operations to improve efficiency. And at this point, there is no clear evidence that Robinhood is replacing laid-off employees with AI.
That said, AI is likely part of the broader trend affecting how companies think about staffing. Rather than completely replacing employees, AI is often used to make existing teams more productive. Tasks involving research, customer support, coding, analysis and administrative work can frequently be handled faster and with fewer people than in the past.
As for service quality, users should probably expect the core user experience to remain largely unchanged. Functions such as trade execution, portfolio tracking, market data and charting are already highly automated.
The areas to watch are customer support and specialized assistance. AI can handle many routine questions effectively, but more complex issues, such as account restrictions, tax-related questions or crypto transfer problems, still benefit from human expertise.
Those concerned about AI taking on too large a role in the crypto space can expect that the future will always involve a human in the loop. AI can automate much of the work, but someone still needs to set the objective.
AI can help analyze information, identify opportunities and execute tasks faster than humans, but it’s ultimately just a tool. Humans decide what level of risk they’re comfortable with, which assets they want exposure to, what yields they’re targeting, what strategies they’re running and how they want capital allocated.
The key takeaway from the staffing changes unfolding at Robinhood isn’t to watch layoffs for investment insights; it’s to watch the broader health of the crypto industry. If companies are expanding, raising capital and hiring aggressively, that’s usually a sign of growing optimism. If layoffs are becoming widespread across the sector, it can be a sign that companies are preparing for tougher conditions ahead and better positioning themselves for the long haul.

People sat with what remained of their belongings on the streets of the Venezuelan capital after homes were levelled by dual earthquakes
Latin America Correspondent
27 June 2026, 15:09 BST
Each morning that Venezuelans wake to the aftermath of the dual earthquakes, it is a little darker, a little grimmer.
It means another night in which prayers for the miraculous recovery of missing loved ones went unanswered, in which the fitful sleep of the survivors is interrupted by nightmares of collapsed buildings and moments of sheer panic.
For ex-policeman Jan Carlos Roa Garcia and his family, it was another night sleeping rough. Their building in Caracas wasn't brought down but is too dangerous to return to.
Tears rolling down his cheeks, he says he's not sure he even knows how to rebuild his family's life again.
"If I was 30 and not 50, then maybe. But I don't know where to begin. And so far, no-one in authority has contacted us."
As a loyal public servant, Jan Carlos was careful not to over-criticise the government's response, exhausted and angry though he is.
Musician Zaira Castro had no such reservations.
"We're all pretty frustrated because the government is not showing what it should â a serious display of help," she says in a plaza just a block away from two collapsed buildings.
"It's actually us, the Venezuelans, who are helping each other. We live in a society that has grown into helping each other. We don't depend on the government â that doesn't exist for us anymore."
In the same part of town, called Chacao, the Interim President, Delcy Rodriguez, took a tour with the mayor and was on the receiving end of residents' ire.
"You're campaigning in the middle of a tragedy! The government isn't doing anything for the people," yelled one resident.
On a personal level, I know these streets well. I lived in the affected neighbourhood of Los Palos Grandes in Chacao for several years when I was the BBC's Venezuela Correspondent. My old apartment block was just metres from the collapsed Petunia building, where rescue crews are working around the clock to reach trapped residents. A friend recently posted on social media that her mother was among the missing under the building's rubble.
It was a huge relief to see my old building, the Alheli, still intact and its genial caretaker, Pedro, still outside chatting to elderly residents on the porch. One of them had twisted her ankle on the way down the building. All of them agreed they couldn't remember a tragedy this severe in Venezuela in their lives.
At the scene of the worst-hit areas â particularly the coastal town of La Guaira â the desperation is even greater. The scene around more than 100 flattened buildings is apocalyptic. And as hopes fade, anger grows.
"There are still people in there, we need machinery," says affected resident Eileen Lada. "Help us, please," she pleads.

This video can not be played
Watch: Newborn baby rescued from Venezuela earthquake rubble
The rescue teams â both Venezuelan and international â have worked through another night showing impressive resilience and focus to try to reach those trapped relatives.
Videos are circulating on social media of the workers successfully pulling out survivors with typical Venezuelan good humour and spirit which bring a lump to the throat.
Rescuers searched for survivors among destroyed buildings throughout the night
The hospitals along the northern coastline are at breaking point. A healthcare system that has been underfunded for decades is now trying to cope with a demand that would be tough for countries with much better infrastructure.
Doctors and nurses are doing what they can in the most trying circumstances most will ever experience in their lives.
And the survivors' stories from inside the wards are chilling.
"It was awful â so many people died, so many family members went missing," Maria Vargas recalled to the AFP news agency from her hospital bed. "I lost my house completely, but we're all right, thank God."
After earthquakes, rescue teams say the first 48 hours are crucial. Those have long since passed. This now feels like the hardest moment in Venezuela's modern history in a country that has had more than its fair share in recent years.

Flights are delayed at Gatwick and Heathrow, with multiple airlines affected (file picture of Gatwick)
27 June 2026, 11:47 BST
Hundreds of flights at London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports have been delayed as the UK's air traffic control service warned disruption is expected to continue into Sunday.
More than 900 inbound and outbound flights at the two travel hubs have been delayed for up to 11 hours and dozens have been cancelled, according to tracker FlightAware, many due to thunderstorms.
NATS, the UK's air traffic control service, said adverse weather conditions meant aircraft needed to "avoid affected areas and be spaced further apart" and this would impact flights for the "remainder of Saturday and overnight".
Gatwick and Heathrow advised passengers to check the status of their flights with airlines before travelling.
More than 474 flights arriving at or departing from Heathrow have been delayed so far, and another 439 in and out of Gatwick, according to FlightAware.
Delays to affected flights vary. Heathrow's live arrival board shows a British Airways flight from Santiago, Chile, that was due to land at 10:00 BST but is now not expected to arrive until 21:00 this evening.
Europe-wide aviation agency
Eurocontrol mapping shows the most severe air traffic control delays in airspace between south-east England and north-western Europe, where the storm clouds are currently located.
However, other UK airports remain largely unaffected.
In an updated statement on Saturday afternoon, NATS said: "Severe thunderstorms across the south east of England and Europe continue to impact flights, and this is expected to continue for the remainder of today and overnight.
"To ensure the safety of the travelling public, aircraft need to avoid affected areas and be spaced further apart, which limits the number of flights that can operate safely.
"We understand disruption is frustrating, but we're working closely with airlines and airports to reduce disruption as much as possible.
"Passengers should continue to contact their airline for the latest information on their flight."
NATS added that the forecast in UK airspace looks generally fine on Sunday, but further thunderstorms are forecast in Europe which may have a further impact on routings across the continent.
The thunderstorms developed overnight - bringing rain and lightning to parts of the UK - following a record-breaking heatwave, with the hottest ever June high of 37.3C recorded in Suffolk on Friday.
Air traffic control mapping showing airspace delays as of 12:50 BST, with delays of less than 15 minutes in blue and more than 45 minutes in red
Passengers grounded for hours
Passenger Adam Joseph, 29, told BBC News that he had been stranded at Venice airport in Italy without air conditioning because his flight to Gatwick had been delayed by four hours and counting.
He was due to depart Venice at 12:30 local time but said the plane had not yet left London on its outbound leg.
"We could've stayed at the hotel for another three to four hours," Joseph said.
"We are also being told that even in the event of a four-hour-plus delay, because of an air traffic control restriction, we will not be entitled to compensation.
"I've had to give up my chair to a family with a pregnant mother.
"People are very angry. We have had no communication from [BA] whatsoever."
BA apologised for the inconvenience, adding: "Like other airlines, we've had to make some adjustments to our schedule today due to air traffic control restrictions caused by adverse weather conditions affecting parts of UK airspace."
Thunderstorms have rocked parts of the UK this week (seen here over Weymouth on Thursday)
Meanwhile, Easyjet passenger Will Poole told the BBC he had cancelled his holiday to the Greek island of Skiathos after his flight from Gatwick was cancelled and moved to Bristol.
He said he boarded at Gatwick shortly after 05:00 on Saturday but was returned to the gate at 11:00.
Mr Poole said he "was eventually offered a complimentary snack and drink after five hours and an email with a Â£6 voucher to spend in Gatwick".
Poole, who booked with Easyjet Holidays, told the BBC he was then offered a replacement flight at 07:00 on Sunday from Bristol Airport, more than 100 miles away.
"In the email it said 'details to follow' about them arranging a transfer, but no mention of a hotel," he said.
"Easyjet staff in the terminal were not very helpful, saying we needed to speak to someone at Easyjet Holidays.
"I got through eventually and decided to cancel the holiday as they couldn't get us on another flight within 12 hours."
Mr Poole said passengers understood the situation was out of Easyjet's control, but "you'd like to think" the replacement flight would have been scheduled from Gatwick. He said he has been promised a refund within 28 days.
Easyjet said that with thunderstorms restricting the number of arrivals and departures, it had to "pre-emptively cancel some flights to and from Gatwick in advance".
It added that it was giving passengers options including refunds, rebookings, hotel accommodation and meals where required.
An amber warning for extreme heat is in place until Sunday morning for parts of eastern and south-east England, while thunderstorms to the south of the UK are forecast to worsen throughout Saturday afternoon.
Eurocontrol said a "broad area of hot, unstable air" stretching from northern Spain to southern Sweden was likely to see further storm-cloud development overnight, adding that there was "a large degree of uncertainty" over when and where they would develop.
A London Gatwick Airport spokesperson said "temporary air traffic restrictions" had been put in place "due to ongoing thunderstorms across the network last night".
A Heathrow Airport spokesperson said "adverse weather conditions" had led to "temporary air traffic restrictions impacting some flights".

Over the last two months the UK has experienced two heatwaves, which have shattered significant, long-standing temperature records.
This hasn't happened since 1911.
And we're still relatively early in the summer with our hottest weather normally coming in late July and into August.
the current June heatwave will gradually come to an end over the weekend
with a return to more average conditions next week, there are already indications that we could see more heatwaves this summer.
It has been a bit of a weather rollercoaster since May when a large area of high pressure - known as a '
' - sat across the UK bringing dry, sunny and very warm weather. A new May record temperature of 35.1C was set in Kew Gardens, London.
June - and the start of meteorological summer - then started on a wet and much cooler note with temperatures dropping to well below average.
Low pressure from the Atlantic brought a series of weather fronts with the whole of June's rainfall in just the first half of the month.
Weather patterns shifted again and in a dramatic turnaround we've just experienced another intense heatwave with the June all-time temperature record broken.
'Significant bursts' of heat are likely
Forecasters issued their
three-month summer outlook
on 1 June which suggested higher-than-normal chances of hotter weather during June.
A "few notable high temperature spikes" are also possible this summer, according to MeteoGroup who currently provide BBC Weather with data.
These seasonal forecasts have so far proved accurate.
For only the second time since their inception in 2021, a red extreme heat warning was issued by the Met Office this week across south-east Wales and southern England.
Schools were closed and the transport network strained as people tried to deal with the extreme heat.
As for the rest of summer - which runs through to the end of August â forecasters suggest "an increased chance of heatwaves and heat-related impacts".
They also say "above-average temperatures" are expected for each month of July and August, and "significant bursts" of heat are expected in the UK, and across Europe.
According to the Met Office, having a hotter summer is now twice as likely than the period of 1991-2020, which is consistent with our warming climate.

Will heatwaves become the new normal?
Human-induced climate change is shifting the baseline temperature higher and this is making our heatwaves hotter, more frequent and longer lasting.
Met Office scientists have said there is an increasing likelihood of extreme temperatures in the UK, revealing that the chance of exceeding 40C is accelerating at pace.
The UK saw the first temperature above 40C in July 2022 when Coningsby, Lincolnshire recorded the UK's all-time highest temperature of 40.3C.
If global warming continues at its current pace, temperatures in the mid-forties could be a serious possibility for the UK by 2050, according to Met Office projections.
In an analysis by World Weather Attribution (WWA), the extreme June heat across Western Europe would have been "impossible just a few decades ago".
Dr Theodore Keeping, an extreme weather and wildfire researcher at Imperial College London, said the link between climate change and worsening heatwaves is "settled".
"Continued fossil-fuel emissions are directly responsible for the disruption people are experiencing this week in their homes, schools and workplaces."
While many of us are used to snow shutting down schools, "this generation is now growing up with 'heat days' as well," he added.
This will only worsen if measures are not taken to reduce emissions.
Dr Akshay Deoras, senior research climate scientist at the University of Reading told BBC Weather: "Unless we drastically cut down the emission of greenhouse gases, global warming is not going to stop. In fact, it will accelerate."
Will a 'Super El NiÃ±o' add extra heat this summer?
-  the climate pattern that pushes up global temperatures - has been officially declared in the Pacific Ocean.
It occurs every two to seven years, lasts for about a year, and typically raises global temperatures up by 0.2C.
Some climate scientists are predicting that the current El NiÃ±o event could develop into a particularly strong - sometimes called '
The US Climate Prediction Center defines a strong El NiÃ±o as sea surface temperatures in the central tropical Pacific +1.5C above the long term average. The last time this happened was during 2015-16 which boosted 2016 to become the hottest year on record at the time.
However, the impact on weather patterns typically lags several months behind the peak of the heating in the Pacific Ocean. So, it is not expected any heatwaves this  summer will be boosted by the current El NiÃ±o event.
For the UK, there is no discernible link between summer heatwaves and El NiÃ±o.
According to Dr James Pope - climate scientist at the Met Office - the most recognised impact of El NiÃ±o on the weather in the UK is to "slightly raise the likelihood of a colder spell during winter".

Andy Burnham will need a "Moscow test" for his policies if he becomes prime minister, the former Chief of the Defence Staff Admiral Sir Tony Radakin has said.
Burnham, the favourite to succeed Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister, has previously said that new legislation must pass a "Makerfield test", the constituency he was elected to this month.
Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, the ex-military chief said the UK's next leader would need to operate "almost like a wartime prime minister" in light of global threats.
Sir Tony's intervention came as the government prepared to publish its long-awaited defence spending plan.
He said that whoever becomes prime minister must fulfil the pledge to increase defence spending to 3.5% of GDP by 2035, describing military capabilities as "too bare".
Negotiations in Whitehall have continued this week over how the Defence Investment Plan (DIP) will be funded, while the government has committed to releasing it before the Nato summit in Turkey on 7 July.
Defence Secretary John Healey and Armed Forces Minister Al Carns - who has not ruled out challenging Burnham to be Labour leader and prime minister -
both resigned from the government earlier this month
over what they said was insufficient investment for the plan.
Speaking to the BBC, Sir Tony said: "As well as having the Makerfield test, I would say it's the Moscow test.
"What do we like to Moscow? Do we look like a strong member of the Nato alliance? Do we look like a strong nuclear power? Do we look like a strong ally of America?
"Because those are the elements that keep us safe."
Asked what his message to Burnham would be should be become prime minister, Sir Tony said: "It is keep our country safe, acknowledge that you have this extraordinary responsibility - so you're almost like a wartime prime minister at the moment.
"And that means you need to invest in what really keeps us safe."
Sir Tony said the UK's level of defence spending at present risked falling "short on those commitments, and then that creates a whole load of hurt with our Nato allies and especially our relationship with America".
Speaking about military capabilities, he said: "We've been very clear in saying that we need to strengthen our armed forces. It means additional money for day to day operations.
"That is stores. That is maintenance. That's how you get those ships out. That's how your aircraft are available for operations. That's how your tanks and armored fighting vehicles are available.
"All of that at the moment is too bare."
Under Sir Keir's leadership, defence spending has increased and the government has pledged, along with most other Nato allies, to increasing spending up to an eventual ambition of 3.5% of GDP by 2035.
But in his resignation statement, Healey said the planned increase set out in the draft DIP fell well short of what was required, and claimed it would in fact lead to operational cutbacks.
There have been reports the Ministry of Defence has asked for an extra Â£28bn between now and the end of the decade, but had only been offered an additional Â£10bn.
All government departments have been asked to cut budgets in order to fund the increase.
Healey's successor Dan Jarvis told BBC South that Burnham "understands the nature and complexity of the world we're operating in, and national security will be, I know, the first priority of any Labour prime minister".
He continued: "I am very confident though there will be a transition in prime minister, the basic policies will remain the same, which is ensuring everything we possibly can to keep the country safe...".
Jarvis also repeated the government's commitment to publishing the DIP before the Nato summit in July.

Ben, from Derby, moved to Russia in 2023 on a private family visa and says he feels safer living there
27 June 2026, 00:02 BST
When Leo Hare moved to Russia from Texas in late 2023, after being granted asylum, he was convinced he was building a better future for his family.
The father of three threw himself into his new life: sampling dumplings , milking goats on a farm and filming videos about life in Russia for his online followers.
Leo is a devout Christian who had become increasingly disillusioned with everything from political division in the US, to genetically modified food and what he sees as the rise of the LGBTQ movement.
At the time, he believed Russia offered an attractive alternative: a society built on Christian faith and family values â a view heavily promoted by the Russian state.
But over time he has also become increasingly concerned about elements such as restrictions on access to information.
He is part of an unlikely migration. As Russia faces international isolation, a few thousand people from countries including Canada, Britain, the United States and parts of Europe are choosing to move there.
Their view of Russia differs sharply from the one many in the West might be familiar with: a country that invaded Ukraine and occupies large parts of it, jails political opponents, places heavy restrictions on civil liberties and faces a raft of international sanctions.
It is an unlikely migration trend - Westerners swapping life in Texas or London for Moscow or Nizhny Novgorod.
Many of the would-be migrants are attracted by Russia's Shared Values visa, sometimes called the "anti-woke" visa, which was introduced a month after Leo was granted asylum.
Introduced by President Vladimir Putin in 2024, the visa offers temporary residency for up to three years to citizens of 47 countries Russia considers "unfriendly".
There is no limit to the number of people who can apply and applicants do not need to pass the usual Russian language, history or law tests.
Instead, they must declare that they share Russia's traditional spiritual and moral values and reject what the Russian government describes as the "destructive neoliberal ideology" of their home countries.
After three years, those on the Shared Values visa must either convert it into a Permanent Residence Permit (PRP) or leave the country. The PRP requires people to sit a language and history exam and more thorough documentation.
Unlike some immigration programmes, the Shared Values visa does not come with housing or financial assistance from the Russian government.
Applicants must pay an administrative fee of 1,600 roubles (Â£17 or $22) and pass medical and criminal records checks.
Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs
Leo Hare (right) at a ceremony granting his asylum which was covered on state TV
Russia says nearly 3,400 people have applied under the scheme as of spring 2026. However, these figures are difficult to verify independently, and do not reveal how many applications were approved.
The visa reflects a broader effort by the Kremlin to present Russia as a defender of traditional values in opposition to what it sees as the moral decline of the West.
In a 2022 decree, Putin warned that Western ideological influence threatened Russian values including marriage and the traditional family and called for Russia to promote a more positive image of itself abroad.
Two years later, the Shared Values visa offered a practical expression of that vision.
An online ecosystem of relocation agencies and influencers promote Russia as a place where family values remain strong and everyday life feels safer.
Ilja Belobragin, general managing partner at Move To Russia, a company which helps foreigners relocate to Russia, says something he frequently hears from his clients is that they "don't recognise the community around me anymore".
Some prospective migrants complain about high immigration in their own countries or what they see as declining living standards, he says.
Russia's war in Ukraine, which has dominated international perceptions of the country since 2022, does not appear to be a decisive factor for many of those making the move.
Some openly support Russia, while others insist their decision is driven by cultural values rather than geopolitics.
Philip Hutchinson helps other people relocate to Russia after moving to Moscow
Philip Hutchinson, a Moscow-based former Conservative Party candidate from the UK who now helps other Westerners relocate to Russia, says he avoids discussing the war.
"What are my thoughts on it? Look, I don't really get involved in that," he says. "I'm not here as a politician. I'm here to live a nice quiet life with my family."
When asked whether helping Westerners relocate to Russia under the Shared Values visa is itself a political act, Philip disagrees.
"We guide a lot of people towards the Shared Values visa because it's the easiest way to become a full resident here right now. It's not political helping people move to Russia."
Following their move to Russia, Leo's family became one of the most visible examples of Western migration.
Russian state media filmed their asylum ceremony and Leo publicly thanked President Putin for welcoming them. At the time, Leo believed he was helping to pioneer what he calls "an unprecedented piece of immigration legislation".
But the reality proved more difficult than he'd anticipated.
Within weeks of arriving, Leo says they were defrauded of 5 million roubles â about Â£52,000 ($66,000) â by a contact they trusted, leaving them homeless.
When I spoke to Leo earlier this year, he was living separately from his wife in the city of Ivanovo, and his older children had returned to the United States.
Asked whether Russia had lived up to his expectations, Leo describes the last two years as the best and worst of his life.
He says he has experienced many sides of Russia: working in an Orthodox monastery, staying in a high-rise apartment and later moving into a small Soviet-era flat. He eventually found work as an English tutor.
He still speaks fondly about ordinary Russians, describing them as generous and welcoming. He praises members of his church community who helped the family survive after they lost their savings and recalls one woman who invited his youngest son into her home and taught him Russian free of charge.
"My heart is just full of love for these people," he says.
But he has also become increasingly concerned about the state of Russia's economy and restrictions on access to information.
Leo is now reconsidering the role he played in promoting Western immigration to Russia.
"I believed in the propaganda," he tells me, admitting that previously he was "the guy who would've written the script".
Although he is committed to staying in Russia out of a sense of "destiny", he now says he misses the freedoms that have shaped the American personality.
"[In] Russia you don't have these human rights values."
Ben doesn't believe Russia is a conservative paradise
Other Westerners who have moved to Russia take issue with how the Shared Values visa itself is being promoted.
Ben - who asked that we use only his first name - moved to Russia in 2023 from Derby in the UK after falling in love with a Russian woman he met through a language exchange website. The couple live in Kursk, near the Ukrainian border.
His family thought he was "a bit insane" for moving to a war zone.
Ben's view of Russia is more nuanced than the one its supporters often portray.
He praises the friendliness of Russians and says he feels safer day to day. At the same time, he rejects the idea that Russia is some kind of conservative paradise.
Ben cites the prevalence of single-parent households, abortion - which he describes as "very widely accepted" - and "extremely high" divorce rates.
"Russia isn't some utopia," he says.
